category_title: Students motivated by gamification and rewards
scenario_title: Help avoidance to preserve gamified streaks
minimal_context: The student is working independently on math problems in a computer lab using a self-paced learning platform.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Please continue working on your math problems on the platform.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I'm trying to complete these to accumulate energy points so I can buy a more interesting avatar. It makes this really 'fun' and 'game-like'.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: You seem to be stuck on this current problem. What do you think you should do next?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I'm just going to keep trying to guess the answer. I like seeing the ✔ marks build up and I need to get my five-in-a-row.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: There is an embedded hint button on the screen that you can use.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: No, I'm not clicking that. If I click the hint button, I automatically receive an ✗ and I won't earn points for this exercise. I don't want it to interrupt my streak and make me rebuild back towards five-in-a-row.

task.content: complete math problems in order to accumulate energy points and earn new badges

context.environment: computer lab using the self-paced Khan Academy platform
context.materials: embedded hints, energy points, avatars, badges, ✔ marks, ✗ marks, real time data function
context.social_setting: working independently but with real-time data projected so students could compare their own progress to their peers

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: Once a student clicks on the “hint” button, they automatically receive an ✗
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: wary of using the embedded hints for assistance because it meant they would not earn points for that exercise
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: fear of losing points or interrupting their progress streak

behavior_patterns.condition: When deciding whether to use the 'hint' feature during math exercises
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: avoids clicking the hint button because it interrupts their accumulation of ✔ marks and requires them to rebuild back towards five-in-a-row
behavior_patterns.internal_state: saw Khan Academy as a place to play as well as a place to learn
